messages.content: Write the engineering culture section of a careers page. Around 250 words.

**Engineering Culture**

Ownership doesn't stop at the pull request here. Most engineers carry a feature from the first design doc through the on-call rotation after launch — if it breaks at 2am, you're the one who picks up. In exchange, you get real say in how the thing gets built.

We keep the bar high on reviews, but nobody waits days for one. Expect a real read within hours. Disagreements get hashed out in a comment thread, not discovered in production three weeks later.

Decisions live in docs, not in someone's head. The team's small enough that anyone could be out the week their answer is needed, so we write it down. New hires read the same design docs the founders wrote on day one.

Late nights happen sometimes. If they happen every sprint, that's a planning problem, not something to be proud of. We'd rather ship something smaller and solid than something big and shaky.

Open any file cold and the reasoning behind it should be obvious. We put real time into tests and tooling so that clarity doesn't have to get rebuilt from scratch by the next person.

If you're looking to write code and walk away, this isn't it. If you want to build something and still be around when it counts, we'd like to talk.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

We keep the review bar high, but nobody waits days for one. Expect a real read within hours. We hash out disagreements in a comment thread, not after they surface in production three weeks later.

Decisions live in docs, not in someone's head. The team is small enough that anyone could be out the week their answer is needed, so we write it down. New hires read the same design docs the founders wrote on day one.

Late nights happen. If they happen every sprint, that's a planning problem, not a badge of honor. We ship something smaller and solid over something big and shaky.

Open any file cold and the reasoning behind it should be obvious. We invest in tests and tooling so the next person doesn't have to rebuild that clarity from scratch.

If you want to write code and walk away, this isn't the place. If you want to build something and still be around when it counts, we should talk.
